subject: cryonics tank
title: What If You Were Frozen After Death? About 200 People Are Waiting in Arizona

scenes.text: What if you were frozen after death, to be woken later? About 200 people already are, in Arizona.
The moment you're declared legally dead, a standby team puts you in an ice bath and restarts your circulation with machines.
Your blood is replaced with preservation fluid, then with chemicals that stop ice crystals forming in your cells.
Over days you're cooled to minus 196 Celsius and lowered into liquid nitrogen. Whole body: 200,000 dollars. Brain only: 80,000.
The first man went in back in 1967. He's still there. A two-year-old girl joined in 2015.
The catch: no one has ever been revived. The company itself says it can't. The customers are betting someone, someday, can.

description:
What if you were frozen after death? At Alcor in Scottsdale, Arizona, about 200 people are stored in liquid nitrogen at minus 196 degrees Celsius, along with around 100 pets.
After legal death, the body is cooled, its blood replaced with preservation fluid and cryoprotectants, then stored in a tank; whole-body preservation costs about 200,000 dollars, a brain alone 80,000. The first patient, frozen in 1967, is still there. No one has ever been revived, and Alcor states that no cryonics organisation can currently do so.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Many scientists call it pseudoscience; one neuroscientist said the brain is far too complex for the process to work. Would you sign up? And what should we run through next?
